ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Chinese Ministry of Public Security's list of sanctioned individuals and entities. PEP screening must cover domestic and foreign PEPs, including family members and close associates, as per FATF recommendations. Enhanced due diligence is required for any match, including source of funds and wealth verification. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and on an ongoing basis using automated systems with full audit trails, and results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the local SAMR online name clearance portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Chinese characters. For foreign-invested enterprises, the name may include a transliteration of the foreign name, but must follow the four-tier naming structure: administrative division, trade name, industry, and organizational form. The trade name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. Phonetic transliteration is permitted but must be approved by the SAMR.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the SAMR within 15 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written explanation of why the name should be accepted, along with supporting evidence such as trademark registrations or prior use. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court within six months. The entire appeal process typically takes 30-60 days, and the applicant may also submit a new name application simultaneously.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are generally not accepted for WFOE registration. The registered address must be a physical location where the company can be reached for official correspondence and where business operations are conducted. Tax authorities and banks require a physical presence for verification. For executive search and headhunting, a physical office is expected to demonstrate commercial substance. Virtual offices may be rejected by the tax bureau and banks, leading to delays or denial of bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: 1. Presence of company nameplate at the registered address. 2. Availability of staff and management during business hours. 3. Evidence of business operations (e.g., client files, contracts, invoices). 4. Compliance with local zoning and business licensing requirements. Risk: Moderate to high, as SAMR and tax authorities conduct unannounced inspections, especially for newly formed entities. Inspections may occur within the first year of operation, and failure to meet physical presence requirements can result in fines or revocation of the business license.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Articles 2, 10, 16, 27, 32, 33, 37, 46, 47, 57 and 58; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2020), Articles 12-18, 26-28
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) at the place of registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Liability Company, together with the Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital; capital subscribed by the sole shareholder must be fully contributed within five years of the establishment date under the 2023 Company Law. There is no blocked escrow account requirement. For executive search and headhunting, no special paid-up capital threshold applies, though the amount should be sufficient to cover initial payroll, rent and licensing cost.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED, a company to be incorporated under the laws of the People's Republic of China (the "Company"), adopted by unanimous written consent on [date] at [place].

WHEREAS, the sole shareholder of the Company has caused the first board of directors meeting to be held to address certain organizational matters. All directors being present, the following resolutions are adopted: 

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE OF SHARE CAPITAL: RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company be, and it hereby is, set at RMB [amount], divided into ordinary shares of RMB [par value] each, fully subscribed by the sole shareholder in accordance with the Articles of Association. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the shareholder's obligation to contribute capital be satisfied in cash or in kind as set forth in the Articles, with the full amount payable no later than five years from the date of issuance of the business license. The directors are authorized to cause a bank to hold any funds only as normal deposit without any escrow limitation unless mandated by law, and to issue a capital contribution receipt upon verification.

2. BANKING AND TREASURY AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company shall open a basic deposit account and a general deposit account at [Bank Name]. ANY TWO of the following authorized signatories, acting jointly, are hereby appointed to sign cheques, wire transfers, loan agreements and other banking instruments: (a) [name, Chairman]; (b) [name, General Manager]; (c) [name, Finance Officer]. The corporate seal attached on each banking instruction shall be attested by the countersignature. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the directors be, and hereby are, authorized to negotiate banking terms, execute account mandates and appoint an online banking administrator.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED, that the registered address of the Company shall be [full address], as disclosed on the business license. The Chairman and the Company Secretary, or any one of them, are authorized to sign the registered office declaration, lease and any utility-related forms. FURTHER RESOLVED, that any change in the registered office shall be approved by the board and filed with the registration authority within applicable statutory periods.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED, that [Name] be, and hereby is, appointed as Chairman of the Board; [Name] be, and hereby is, appointed as General Manager and Legal Representative; [Name] be, and hereby is, appointed as Chief Financial Officer; and [Name] be, and hereby is, appointed as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board. Their respective powers and duties are those established in the Articles of Association and the applicable Company Law.

5. EXECUTION MEANS: RESOLVED, that any two of the Chairman, General Manager and Company Secretary may execute all documents, including the incorporation application, capital verification documents and any consents necessary to carry out these resolutions.

The above resolutions are recorded as the unanimous act of the Board and shall bind the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Corporate Information Pre-Collected via One-Stop Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) through the Unified Enterprise Registration Self-Service Platform (e.g. Shanghai 'One-Stop Enterprise Start-up' portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The authorized shareholder or its appointed notarized agent shall first log into the local MSA online portal and select the 'Enterprise Establishment Registration' module. The applicant must complete the autonomous name declaration by entering potential simplified Chinese name, industry description (e.g. 'Human Resource Management Consulting' or 'Executive Search'), proposed business scope, shareholder identity, registered capital amount and contribution period. The system will automatically screen the name database for identical or confusingly similar names, prohibited words, and restricted industry terms. Once the name is pre-approved, an electronic 'Name Acceptance Notice' is generated and reserved for six months. Simultaneously, the system pre-fills the unified social credit code, enabling the applicant to proceed directly to the next filing step.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID copy of foreign sole shareholder
Choice of two candidate company names (Chinese and English)
Draft business scope in alignment with ISIC 7830
Registered capital amount and contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to identical or high-similarity conflict, the applicant may file an online re-submission with a 1-day automatic clearing window or provide a letter of authorization from the conflicting registrant. If the system flags prohibited terms, the applicant must delete those terms and re-submit; manual review by the MSA is available within two additional working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Application, Articles of Association and Investment Information Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Market Supervision Administration (MSA) corporate registration window or the same Unified Enterprise Registration Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant must complete and submit the formal 'Application for Establishment Registration of a Company', accompanied by the fully executed Articles of Association, proof of registered office (a lease contract and landlord's property certificate or an official letter of address suitability), identity documents of the legal representative and supervisor, and the board appointments resolution. For a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, the system simultaneously captures the Foreign Investment Information Report and automatically transmits it to the Ministry of Commerce; no separate visit to the commerce window is required. All shareholder signatures, director appointments and legal representative consent must be effected by advanced electronic signature or by physical identity verification at a self-service terminal. The registration officer performs a formal and limited substantive review of the documents. Upon approval, the unified social credit code is confirmed and the business license will be prepared.
required_dossiers: Duly signed Application for Establishment Registration
Original/notarized passport or corporate certificate of the sole shareholder
Articles of Association executed by the shareholder
Registered office proof (lease contract + property ownership certificate or land use certificate)
Appointment documents for legal representative, directors, supervisor and general manager
Identity copies of all statutory officers
Foreign Investment Information Report form (embedded in the application)
Consent letter from the foreign investor to the proposed legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or queried, the MSA issues a 'Notice of Corrections'. The applicant has seven working days to upload corrective documents; if the correction is timely, the 4-day SLA restarts from the resubmission date. In case of a substantive rejection involving business scope or foreign investment restricted category, the applicant may appeal to the same MSA or re-file with a revised scope. Failing that, a written petition for administrative review can be lodged with the higher-level administration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Business License, Company Seal Carving and Multi-Purpose Registration Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration business license issuance counter and Public Security Department sanctioned seal engraving shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon final approval, the MSA issues the 'Business License for a Limited Liability Company' in both original and duplicate copies, with the company's name, registered capital, legal representative, establishment date and unified social credit code. Through the 'one license with multiple certificates' institutional reform, the MSA automatically forwards the registration data to the tax authority, social insurance agency, housing provident fund centre and statistics bureau, eliminating need for separate filings. Immediately after receiving the license, the company must engage a Public Security Department licensed seal engraving vendor to produce the company chop, financial seal, legal representative seal, invoice seal and contract seal. Each seal is electronically recorded into the national seal database with a unique engraving filing number within 24 hours. No company operations may commence until the license and seals are physically obtained and the entity's bank account is operative.
required_dossiers: Original special stamped receipt of license issuance
Legal representative ID card or passport
Seal engraving service entrustment letter
Copy of the Business License and unified social credit code certificate
Power of attorney from the sole shareholder appointing the local agent for seal collection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal engraving shop rejects the order due to an address or identity anomaly, the applicant must settle the mismatch with the MSA through a formal 'Correction of Registered Data' application and re-submit the seal order. If a data mismatch occurs in the multi-purpose registration feed, the applicant should obtain a written confirmation letter from MSA and present it to the bank or tax office for manual resynchronization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Capital Contribution Receipt, and Tax/Social Registration Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in mainland China (e.g. Bank of China, ICBC, CMB) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the direct bank reporting channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is issued and company seals are in hand, the legal representative or an authorized officer must appear in person at a bank branch to open the basic deposit account ('Grundlegerkonto') and, if required, a general deposit account. The bank requires the original business license, the company chop, legal representative ID, the Articles of Association, and a resolution from the first board meeting designating authorized signatories. Once the account is opened, the bank issues an 'Account Opening Notice' and uploads the information to the People's Bank of China payment system. For the foreign shareholder remitting capital, the bank acts as the agent for SAFE's direct investment registration and logs the inward remittance against the foreign exchange code. Upon receipt of capital, the company must issue a capital contribution certificate to the shareholder and record the paid-in amount in the national enterprise credit information system. Finally, verify that the tax registration has been automatically activated; if not, attend the tax authority self-service terminal to print the tax payer qualification and complete any subsequent electronic invoice application.
required_dossiers: Original Business License (both original and duplicate for verification)
Company chops (company chop, finance chop, legal representative chop)
Identity documents of all account signatories
First board resolution appointing bank signatories
Articles of Association and name acceptance notice
Foreign Investment Information Report completion code
SAFE/PBOC registration forms (provided by bank)
Capital contribution schedule and shareholder certificate template
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening due to incomplete documentation, the applicant has five working days to obtain the missing certificate and re-apply at the same branch or choose an alternate bank. If the SAFE registration code takes longer than expected, the bank may open the account without the code but restrict foreign currency receipts; the legal counsel should request an expedited SAFE review through the bank's foreign exchange desk and ensure the filing is submitted within two working days. If tax registration fails to synchronise, the company should print and submit a manual 'Tax Registration Application' at the local tax hall and provide the unified social credit code certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA). Online electronic portal: National Electronic Tax Bureau (E-Tax Bureau) of the State Taxation Administration, accessible through provincial-level E-Tax Bureau portals, the 12366 Taxpayer Service Platform, and Golden Tax Phase IV infrastructure for registration, filing, invoice management, and export tax-refund administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the China Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE): (1) Complete formation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); the Business License contains the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). (2) Under PRC law, the USCC is the sole statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) for Enterprise Income Tax, VAT, and all other PRC taxes; no separate VAT identification number is issued. (3) SAMR automatically transmits registration data to the State Taxation Administration, which opens the taxpayer file; the WFOE must then complete tax registration particulars in the E-Tax Bureau (legal representative, accounting method, industry classification, bank deposit account, shareholder details) before the first filing period. (4) For cross-border service export involving a zero-rating claim, the WFOE must preserve offshore service contracts and complete any required tax-exemption or zero-rating record-filing with the in-charge tax authority before issuing a zero-rated electronic invoice. (5) For a foreign non-resident entity, including the Hong Kong parent, without a permanent establishment in China, no PRC VAT registration number is ordinarily issued; where such a non-resident makes taxable supplies in China, the domestic recipient is the VAT withholding agent. (6) If a non-resident entity performs a physical project or maintains a taxable establishment in China, it must complete an Organization Temporary Registration with the in-charge tax authority and will be assigned a temporary 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code/TIN for the duration of the activity. All steps are concluded through the E-Tax Bureau portal; no physical visit is generally required except biometric verification of the legal representative or person in charge for high-risk cases.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide a check-the-box election or any elective transparent-entity classification. The WFOE is statutorily a PRC resident limited-liability enterprise subject to entity-level Enterprise Income Tax on worldwide income. Hybrid mismatch and pass-through elections are not available. A VAT status election between small-scale taxpayer and general VAT taxpayer status exists for VAT qualification only and does not alter entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China, governed by the Interim Regulations on Value-Added Tax and the comprehensive VAT reform framework (Caishui [2016] No. 36). Executive search/headhunting services supplied by the WFOE are classified as modern/cognition services and are generally subject to the 6 percent VAT rate; the PRC headline goods rate is 13 percent.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory when cumulative taxable turnover over any rolling 12-month period exceeds RMB 5,000,000. A taxpayer below that threshold is treated as a small-scale VAT taxpayer; under the current temporary policy through December 31, 2027, small-scale taxpayers with monthly taxable sales not exceeding RMB 100,000 are exempt from VAT. Voluntary registration as a general VAT taxpayer is permitted if the taxpayer has a sound accounting system and satisfies the conditions set by the State Taxation Administration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The PRC operates Golden Tax Phase IV and the Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice system. Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoices are issued through the National Electronic Tax Bureau; invoice data is pushed to the tax authority in real time, invoice numbers and digital XML files are centrally allocated, and VAT special invoices are authorized and verified through the National VAT Invoice Verification Platform. There is no separate physical fiscal stamp; anti-fraud controls consist of real-time taxpayer data integration, invoice number and code verification, and reconciliation of invoice amount, tax rate, tax amount, contract terms, fund

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) / State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China legally subscribes to current-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) may freely receive and pay for services and trade on current account, but every transaction must clear SAFE's transaction-by-transaction verification system and the submitting bank's internal control. The Hong Kong parent's capital injection (registered capital) is treated as a capital-account inflow and must be routed into a designated foreign exchange capital account opened at a SAFE-jurisdiction bank. Such funds cannot be used unless the bank has performed foreign exchange registration and the enterprise has provided a genuine and reasonable use plan. Current-account conversion into RMB is allowed without a specific quantitative cap; banks rely on the beneficial informational and documentation basis. Profit repatriation for the WFOE is subject to three sequential hurdles: (i) completion of the annual statutory audit by a PRC CPA firm, (ii) final settlement of corporate income tax and any withholding taxes on dividends with the tax authority, and (iii) formal determination and payment of the dividend under the Foreign Investment Law and SAFE's Foreign Exchange Registration for Direct Investment. There is no mandatory surrender ratio for current-account receipts, but all foreign exchange collected from export or service proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic foreign currency settlement account and be reported under the cross-border payment monitoring system. Offshoreholding and trade structures cannot be used to circumvent these controls without facing administrative penalties and mandatory bank-account restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For current-account merchandise and service receipts, the WFOE must repatriate the foreign exchange proceeds into its domestic foreign currency settlement account within 90 days from the customs declaration date (goods) or the invoice date (services), as monitored by SAFE's trade and payment verification database. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0% — there is no compulsory surrender into RMB; instead, the WFOE may elect to keep the proceeds in foreign currency, convert them to RMB, or use them to pay current-account obligations, provided every usage is verified against the original transaction documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low as primary treasury rail, but possible as a supplementary payment actuator. Under current NFRA and SAFE rules, offshore digital EMIs such as Wise and Revolut are not licensed to hold deposit accounts for mainland Chinese legal entities, cannot settle CNY through CIPS, and cannot provide the required foreign exchange registration and verification. They are legally barred from opening a principal bank account for a WFOE. The WFOE may only instruct a licensed domestic bank to execute cross-border wires; if the bank maintains no direct SWIFT relation with the EMI, the transaction will be routed through a correspondent. Accordingly, the WFOE's operational treasury must be domiciled in a Chinese Tier-1 commercial bank, and Wise/B2B rails may only support secondary outbound margin payments where the beneficiary holds an account at the EMI and the underlying contract is fully documented.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The PRC corporate account-opening framework mandates physical presence. The WFOE's legal representative, or a duly authorized general manager/executive, must appear in-branch at the account-opening bank for a live KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by domestic banks; a power of attorney must be notarized and apostilled/legalized for PRC use, but the attorney-in-fact, if not the legal representative, still needs to be physically present with the principal's original identification. Shanghai Free Trade Zone pilots and certain banks allow video interviews, but the branch retains the right to require an in-person session at the account-opening stage. All documents for foreign shareholders must be translated into Chinese by a qualified translation agency, and the bank will conduct a secondary call-back verification with the legal representative during onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Indirect beneficial ownership through the Hong Kong shell parent, where the ultimate individual owners cannot be immediately identified from the WFOE's Articles of Association.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of the Hong Kong company's Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, NAR1 annual return, full share register, registered agent's certificate, and a notarised UBO declaration for each natural person holding 25% or more of the WFOE via the Hong Kong parent; passport copies and recent utility bills for all UBOs; and a written explanation of capital-sourcing and source-of-funds for the registered capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cross-border retainer payments from jurisdictions with weak AML enforcement or from politically exposed persons in the executive placement sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening report against UN, EU, UK OFSI, US OFAC, and China's sanction list for every retainer payer and candidate invoice; completed PEP assessment forms; executed search agreements containing the client's identity, purpose of the retainer, and fee schedule; and in-depth due-diligence files on any headhunting partner receiving a commission split.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cash-like, below-threshold deposits or statement of retained fees that do not match the headhunting agency's documented recruitment milestones and final placement success.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Milestone-based retainer schedule with supporting correspondence, interview notes, final placement offer letters signed by the client, commission invoices, and the WFOE's revenue-recognition policy under ASBE/IFRS; bank statements for six months plus a reconciliation signed by the WFOE's CFO and external accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected diversion of capital injection into working capital or client fee reimbursement rather than WFOE business expansion, especially in the first six months after establishment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE-registered Foreign Exchange Direct Investment Registration Certificate, capital verification report issued by a PRC CPA, the approved capital use plan, payroll records and social security contributions for employees, office lease invoices, and a board resolution confirming the purpose of each capital-account disbursement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong parent injects registered capital via SWIFT MT103 wire to the WFOE's foreign exchange capital settlement account at a SAFE-designated Tier-1 bank. The payment instruction must include the transaction purpose code '622 - Direct investment in mainland China' (or the current SAFE trade code), the reference 'Registered Capital Injection under the Foreign Investment Law', and the SAFE foreign exchange registration number of the WFOE. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the inbound vesting against the Foreign Investment Negative List and requires the WFOE to present the capital-account opening notice, incorporation certificate, and the lease/purchase contract for the registered office. A PRC CPA must subsequently issue a capital verification report within 30 days of injection; any later conversion of the foreign currency into RMB must be made only for genuine operating expenses, with supporting invoices, and must be reported to SAFE.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For services provided to overseas clients, outbound payments from the WFOE include subcontractor fees, licensing fees, and IT infrastructure costs. The primary clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 wire from the WFOE's domestic foreign currency settlement account, supported by a copy of the service contract, the original invoice, proof of service completion, and the withholding tax certificate if the recipient is a PRC tax resident subject to the tax treaty. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are unsuitable for executive-search services because they require transport documents or a bill of lading; they may be used only if the WFOE expands into tangible recruitment merchandising (e.g., test kits, executive assessment products). For such physical goods, we would advise a sight LC through the issuing bank plus a documentary collection for smaller suppliers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD deliverable forwards with real trade/current-account underlying, approved by a SAFE-designated bank
Onshore foreign currency swaps for current-account cashflow management
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for hedging foreign-currency loan interest/principal exposure
Peripheral boundary: NDFs are not permissible for onshore WFOEs; only the Hong Kong parent may participate in offshore NDF markets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after the anniversary date of incorporation of the private limited company; the return is made up to the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration fees escalate: HK$420 (USD 53.85) for delivery more than 42 days but not more than 3 months; HK$840 (USD 107.69) for 3-6 months; HK$1,260 (USD 161.54) for 6-9 months; HK$1,680 (USD 215.38) for 9-12 months. If the annual return is not delivered within 12 months, the company and each responsible officer commit an offence and are liable to a fine of HK$50,000 (USD 6,410) plus a continuing daily fine of HK$1,000 (USD 128). The Registrar may also commence administrative strike-off of the company's name under section 744 of the Companies Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the date of business registration; the Business Registration Office issues a renewal demand note about one month before expiry, and payment is due before the expiration date of the current certificate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a penalty of up to HK$300 (USD 38.46) imposed by the Registrar. Carrying on business without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence punishable by a fine of HK$5,000 (USD 641) and imprisonment for one year under the Business Registration Ordinance Cap 310.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) with audited financial statements and tax computations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the date stated in the return, generally one month after the issue date; electronic filing through eTAX may be granted an extension to about three months. The IRD issues Form BIR51 to active companies annually, usually in April for year-end 31 December companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse may result in a fine of up to HK$10,000 (USD 1,282) on conviction under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; if the failure is continuing, the court may impose a daily fine of HK$700 (USD 89.74) for repeat offences, and the IRD may issue estimated assessments that become final if not contested. Unpaid resultant tax attracts interest (8% p.a.) and a 5% surcharge if unpaid after six months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A and individual IR56B forms)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the issue date of the return; for the year of assessment, the standard due date is 1 May (or the date specified in the notice) for all employees, directors, and executive search consultants who were compensated during the period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is an offence carrying a fine of up to HK$5,000 (USD 641) on first conviction, with a daily fine of HK$500 (USD 64.10) for continuing offences, in addition to any charge of tax evasion under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employment Agency Licence Renewal (mandatory for executive search and headhunting business)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Application for renewal must be submitted not earlier than 4 months and not later than 28 days before the licence expiry date; the licence is ordinarily valid for 1 year and renewable annually upon continuing compliance with the Employment Ordinance Cap 57.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the renewal is not filed within the statutory window, the licence lapses. Operating without a valid licence is an offence under section 52 of the Employment Ordinance, punishable by a fine of up to HK$50,000 (USD 6,410) and imprisonment for six months; the Labour Department may also reject a renewal application where there are grounds under the licensing regime.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Hong Kong private limited company is required to have its financial statements audited by an independent Certified Public Accountant (CPA) registered under the Accounting and Financial Reporting Council unless it qualifies for the audit exemption under the Companies Ordinance (Cap 622). The exemption applies to a 'small private company' (or a member of a 'small private company group') satisfying at least two of the following three quantitative criteria for the financial year: (i) total annual revenue does not exceed HK$10,000,000 (USD 1,282,051); (ii) total assets at the end of the financial year do not exceed HK$10,000,000 (USD 1,282,051); and (iii) the average number of employees during the year does not exceed 100. Once a company exceeds two of the thresholds (e.g., revenue over HK$10 million and assets over HK$10 million), a mandatory CPA audit is triggered. A statutory audit is also mandatory for companies that are members of a group unless the group qualifies as a small private company group. Audit exemption is never available for banks, insurance companies, securities dealers, licensed leveraged foreign exchange traders, or any company whose constitutional documents require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA); eligible small private companies may instead apply the HKFRS for Private Entities (also known as the SME-FRS / HKFRS for Private Entities). The independent statutory audit, when required, must be conducted in accordance with Hong Kong Standards on Auditing (HKSA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong has no separate annual UBO filing requirement. The company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) under Part 17 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap 622), recording any individual with significant control (i.e., holding more than 25% of the shares or voting rights, the right to appoint or remove a majority of the directors, or otherwise exercising significant influence or control). The SCR must be updated within 7 days after the company becomes aware of any change. The Annual Return (Form NAR1) filed with the Companies Registry constitutes the annual confirmation of members, shareholders and directors. For share transfers, the instrument of transfer must be lodged with the company and the Register of Members updated within 2 months of lodgment; there is no 30-day reporting window to the Companies Registry for ordinary share transfers. Allotments of new shares require a Return of Allotment (Form NSC1) to the Companies Registry within 1 month.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 1,200 per annum for registered office address, company secretary and statutory register maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 15,000 per annum depending on turnover, transaction volume, and number of subsidiaries

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard 25% headline rate; small-scale low-profit enterprises may benefit from a reduced effective rate of 5% where annual taxable income does not exceed RMB 3 million, assets do not exceed RMB 50 million and employees do not exceed 300; High-and-New-Technology Enterprises are eligible for a 15% preferential rate; additional 100% R&D expense deduction is available for qualifying recruitment tech and database development; no patent-box regime applies to pure executive search fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Main Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, Class A) together with supporting schedules including A105000, A105080, A107014 and related-party transaction forms; filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal (electronic tax bureau).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed and final CIT settled within 5 months after the end of the fiscal year (for a calendar-year entity, on or before 31 May of the following year); quarterly provisional returns and prepayments are due within 15 days after the close of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from the headhunting agency's provision of C-suite executive search and specialist technical recruitment services, including retained wire fees and success fees billed during the tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue attributable to the PRC WFOE under domestic tax law. If any portion of revenue relates to an overseas engagement but the service is performed or managed from China, the full worldwide income is taxable in China. Restatements for transfer-pricing purposes are made through the related-party transaction schedules and not below Box 1. No deduction is allowed for a notional service fee charged by the Hong Kong parent unless supported by valid arm's length documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to headhunting revenue, including salaries of active talent consultants, database subscription fees, background-check costs and traceable engagement costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border cost recharges from the Hong Kong parent (e.g., centrally incurred marketing or administrative overheads) must meet arm's length standards and be evidenced by time records, invoices and bank wires; otherwise the tax authority may disallow the expense and make a special tax adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-period taxes and surcharges such as urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges and stamp duty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT is not deductible in the CIT return but associated surcharges may be deducted; for cross-border revenues, zero-rating or exemption of VAT on export services applies only where the services are consumed wholly outside China and proper proof is archived.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales and marketing expenses of the executive search business, including overseas business development travel, client entertainment and candidate marketing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Business entertainment is deductible only up to 60% of actual expenses, capped at 0.5% of revenue. Overseas marketing costs must be supported by foreign invoices, transaction trails and evidence of a genuine outbound business purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General and administrative expenses, office rent, compliance licensing fees (HR service license), legal and professional fees, and office-related overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees charged by a non-resident related party are deductible only where the services were actually rendered, the expense confers a direct and identifiable benefit on the WFOE, and the price is at arm's length; pure profit-distribution style management fees are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense on bank borrowings and intercompany loans, exchange losses, and financing charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a Hong Kong related lender must respect the thin-capitalization ratio of 2:1 unless the arm's length nature is proven; cross-border interest is subject to statutory withholding tax (10%) with a potential 7% treaty rate under the PRC-Hong Kong DTA, and treaty relief must be documented before or at the time of withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bad debts, impairment of accounts receivable and other required impairment charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Unrealized impairments on related-party receivables are generally not deductible; an actual economic loss supported by documentation and formal abandonment is required for deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result after deducting operating costs, expenses, taxes, impairments and adding investment income and changes in fair value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This accounting line is the starting point for tax reconciliation. Special tax adjustments, including transfer pricing corrections, must be reflected on the relevant schedules that feed into the taxable income computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax after adding non-operating income and deducting non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder should note that book profit reported here forms the basis for future dividend distribution; CIT must be settled before dividends are paid, and subsequent outbound remittance triggers separate dividend withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal taxable income after adding and deducting permanent and temporary differences, exempt income, additional deductions (including R&D super-deduction) and tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the line on which the 25% headline rate is applied. Distributions made to the Hong Kong parent are subject to a separate 10% dividend withholding tax (5% under PRC-HK DTA on qualifying holdings) and are reported on withholding tax returns, not on the annual CIT return itself.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts administrative fines under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law ranging from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious noncompliance, plus a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of overdue tax per day under Article 32. Underreporting causing underpayment of tax is treated as tax evasion under Article 63, subject to recovery, surcharge, and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. Willful false filing can be referred for criminal liability under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law where the amount evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax due, exposing the offender to imprisonment of up to 7 years for large amounts; additional joint punishment consequences include tax-dishonesty blacklisting and travel restrictions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the reduced 5% dividend withholding rate under Article 10 of the PRC-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement, the Hong Kong shareholder must: (i) be the beneficial owner and directly hold at least 25% of the capital of the PRC WFOE; (ii) obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Inland Revenue Department; (iii) file the Chinese non-resident treaty benefit claim form with the competent Chinese tax authority before the payment date or within the prescribed filing period; (iv) provide a beneficial-ownership declaration confirming the Hong Kong entity has substance, real decision-making power, and no contractual or legal obligation to pass on the dividend; and (v) maintain supporting documentation such as board minutes, employment records, office lease, bank statements and group organizational charts. If the reduced rate is not approved in advance, the WFOE must withhold at 10% and the Hong Kong resident may file for a refund of the excess withholding within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate on cross-border interest and royalties is 10% for non-resident enterprises without treaty protection. Under the PRC-Hong Kong DTA, interest is capped at 7% and royalties at 7% of gross payments, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and holds a valid HK Tax Residency Certificate. Intercompany software licensing fees, subscriber database royalties and headhunting method royalties are eligible for the 7% treaty rate only where there is genuine licensed property and active substance; failure to satisfy these conditions will re-trigger the statutory 10% rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under State Taxation Administration Announcement No. 42 of 2016, contemporaneous Local File documentation is mandatory where annual related-party transactions exceed: RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers, and RMB 100 million for service transactions (including executive-search management recharges). A Master File is required where the group's consolidated revenue exceeds RMB 5 billion and the Chinese entity has cross-border related-party transactions above the documentation de-minimis thresholds; transfer-pricing policy documentation should be prepared on a conservative basis whenever cross-border fees are involved.
